_comment: Plinth is a gallery plinth under soft top light: the item is the exhibit and everything around it is styled. The mark, palette, headlines, kickers and feature copy are the slot's identity declaration.
_mark: Lightfold: a print standing on a lit plinth. The bright paper print overlaps its plinth's lit amber cap, which overlaps a darker amber-deep body, so the three read as one glyph under one light. Original slot-owned geometry, not a font character or library glyph. Every shape is a rounded plate or a disc because the icon gate measures each role's medial width: a faceted polygon tapers to nothing at its corners and is refused as a 2px stroke. LIGHTFOLD in scripts/lib/icon_design.py, the launcher layers and the in-app brand glyph share the same four paths on the 108dp grid.
_palette: Cool graphite and paper frame a muted teal action color, a deeper teal lane and a soft mist container. Pine provides quiet emphasis so product photos, not chrome, lead the colour. Error reds are semantic; product-photo backdrop choices remain separate from UI identity. PlinthPalette in Color.kt uses exactly this identity set.
_claim_bounds: The app preserves item pixels in Original mode, styles backgrounds around the item, checks marketplace rules, applies a saved look across batches and slide series, lets sellers set text, and exports marketplace packs. It shows cost before paid actions; it does not claim that generated imagery is original photography.
_headlines: Six short, truthful lines for the screenshot journey over the Studio screen: the seller's own photo, the priced tool grid, the background and lighting tools, the composition tools, the wider export entry and the one-credit cut-out. Every line describes a tool entry point with its cost shown; none claims a generated result.
featureTagline: Keep the item's pixels. Style everything around it.
